newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK retailer Theme to expand into U.S., S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: HK retailer Theme to expand into U.S., S.Korea.

text.p: Hong Kong fashion retailer Theme International Holdings Ltd plans to expand into the United States and South Korea by the end of 1997 and will issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) soon to raise its profile.

In a "Blueprint for 1997" released on Tuesday, Theme forecast more than 600 retail points of sale by the year 2000, with 260 in China, Hong Kong and Macau. Existing networks in Canada, Japan, Taiwan and Southeast Asia would be expanded.
The first point of sale in South Korea and the United States would be set up in the fall/winter season in 1997 under distributorship, the company said. Distributors have not yet been chosen, it said.
With an eye on raising its profile in the United States the company will issue ADRs of its shares soon, having received U.S. regulatory approval earlier this year.
The value of the ADRs will not be huge, however.
"The purpose is not for raising finance but for marketing purposes," said Louis Liu, an adviser to company management.
The ADR issue will also "pave the way" for Theme's 40-percent owned associate Fitlady Investment Holdings Ltd to be floated on NASDAQ later in the year, the company said.
Theme bought its stake in Fitlady, a Hong Kong-based firm which manufactures women's stockings and hosiery products in China, in May 1996 for HK$120 million ($15.4 million).
It outlined plans on Tuesday to merge Fitlady with Beijing-based socks manufacturer Mega Concord (China) Investment Ltd in April 1997.

The merger, which Theme said would make Fitlady the largest socks and hosiery maker in Asia, would dilute Theme's stake in the operation to 32 percent, although that holding might be topped up before the U.S. listing.
The merged company's offering would be aimed at raising funds for expansion of existing operations.
"We want to make it a total vertical factory," Theme chairman Kenneth Lai told a news conference.
Details of the offering have yet to be worked out.
Theme said Fitlady had interim net profits of HK$39.5 million ($5.06 million) on turnover of HK$124 million ($15.9 million) for the six months ended September 30, 1996.

The net profit of Theme in the period was $51.03 million ($6.5 million) against a HK$0.92 million ($117,900) loss in the same period the year before, on turnover of HK$400.8 million ($51.4 million) against HK$329.3 million ($42.2 million) the year before.
